record.paper_title: Some open problems in mathematical relativity
record.original_question: If an asymptotically flat spacetime has a Cauchy surface without horizons, must the spacetime contain a maximal Cauchy hypersurface?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $(M,g)$ be a smooth, time-oriented, globally hyperbolic, asymptotically flat spacetime of dimension $3+1$ satisfying the dominant energy condition. Recall that a Cauchy hypersurface $\Sigma \subset M$ is a smooth spacelike hypersurface that is met exactly once by every inextendible causal curve in $M$. The hypersurface $\Sigma$ is said to be "without horizons" if it contains no apparent horizons, i.e., no compact two-surface in $\Sigma$ on which the outgoing null expansion vanishes (so $\Sigma$ contains no trapped or marginally trapped surfaces). A Cauchy hypersurface $\Sigma$ is called maximal if its mean curvature (with respect to the future-pointing unit normal in $M$) vanishes identically, and $\Sigma$ is asymptotic at spatial infinity to a hyperplane of constant time in the asymptotic Minkowski coordinates.

Question: If $(M,g)$ admits a Cauchy hypersurface without horizons (in the sense above), must $(M,g)$ contain a maximal Cauchy hypersurface?
artifact.status_search_result: Existence of maximal hypersurfaces in asymptotically flat spacetimes is classically addressed by Bartnik's interior-barrier construction (1984) and subsequent work, but a general theorem asserting existence whenever the spacetime has a Cauchy surface free of (apparent) horizons does not appear in the literature. Surveys of open problems in mathematical relativity list this as an unresolved question, and no proof or counterexample is found in available sources.

status_evidence.title: Existence of maximal surfaces in asymptotically flat spacetimes
status_evidence.snippet: Existence of maximal surfaces in asymptotically flat spacetime satisfying an interior condition is proven.
status_evidence.claim: Existence results require an interior barrier condition; not a clean horizon-free hypothesis.

status_evidence.title: Maximal Surfaces and General Relativity (Bartnik)
status_evidence.snippet: In asymptotically flat spacetimes, maximal surfaces play a role analogous to CMC slicings; existence relies on barrier constructions.
status_evidence.claim: General existence of maximal Cauchy hypersurfaces under merely a no-horizon assumption remains unproved.
